title: Henri Poincaré's birth chart
metaDescription: Henri Poincaré's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 8.8° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Five of the nine placements whose signs are settled fall in earth signs — at least half of what the unknown hour leaves certain. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 8.8° into Taurus — the first decan, which the old scheme hands to Venus. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Aries (13.3°), Venus in Pisces (23.2°), Mars in Virgo (0.4°): thought that arrives already in motion, attraction that works by atmosphere, effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mars and Saturn hold the closest angle here — a square, 1.4° wide. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, Mars trine Pluto at 2.0°, and Uranus sextile Neptune at 3.0° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Mercury makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. Venus in Pisces at 23.2° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Capricorn at 27.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. The table describes circumstance rather than quality — a planet in detriment is inconvenienced, not diminished.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements earth 5, water 2, fire 1, air 1; modalities mutable 4, fixed 3, cardinal 2. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Every body was moving forward that day — no apparent reversals anywhere in the chart.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Taurus into Gemini during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.1° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
